newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ANA plans 777s for expanding Japan-HK rout.
newsitem.headline: ANA plans 777s for expanding Japan-HK rout.

text.p: All Nippon Airways(ANA) is planning to introduce new, high capacity Boeing 777 aircraft on its Japan-Hong Kong routes as part of a 26 per cent expansion in international capacity, a company spokesman told Reuters.
The airline, Japan's largest domestic carrier, is also applying for Government approval to increase the number of flights between Hong Kong and Osaka.
ANA began daily flights from Hong Kong to Osaka on July 15 last year using Boeing 767-300ER aircraft. It also operates daily Boeing 747 flights between the territory and Tokyo.

ANA said its first of three Boeing 777s due to be delivered this autumn will be introduced progressively on services from Narita to Hong Kong and Beijing and from Kansai to Hong Kong, Singapore and Shanghai.
However the final seat and cargo configuration has still to be decided, the spokesman added.

The airline's recently published business plan said that:" With tourist demand for Hong Kong reaching unprecedented levels as a result of events surrounding the colony's return to China, ANA has seen the popularity of its Hong Kong services increase dramatically."

"In response, frequencies from Kansai to Hong Kong will be increased over the coming year, pending government approval. When combined with operations from Narita, services to Japan from Hong Kong will become the carrier's largest market served from Japan," the plan said.
ANA also hopes to start services to one more destination in China in addition to the existing cities of Beijing, Shanghai, Dalian and Qingdao.

The carrier is forecasting it will carry more than 40 million passengers this year along with 130,000 tonnes of international and 385,000 tonnes of domestic cargo as part of a third year of rapid growth.
